faults.name: Latency & jitter
faults.simulates: A slow MCP server or a congested host: the call succeeds, but late.
faults.mechanism: The proxy holds the call for the configured delay, then forwards it to the real MCP server.
faults.reversal: Instant. Calls stop being delayed on the next request.
guardrails: Delay never exceeds 5 s per call
Ceiling on share of calls from the policy
faults.limitation: Adds delay in the backend, not on the network, so transport buffering effects are not reproduced.

faults.name: Timeout · no response
faults.simulates: An MCP server that accepts the request and never answers.
faults.mechanism: The proxy waits, then raises the same timeout error the MCP client raises. The real call is never made.
faults.limitation: The wait is shorter than the client's real 20 s timeout so experiments stay fast; the error type is identical.

faults.name: Server error
faults.simulates: The tool runs and reports is_error=true (an internal failure on the server).
faults.mechanism: The proxy answers with an MCP tool error in place of the server. The real call is never made.
faults.limitation: Errors are not retryable by contract, so a pass here mostly measures graceful degradation.

faults.name: Rate limit · retry-after
faults.simulates: A dependency enforcing a quota and telling the caller when to come back.
faults.mechanism: The proxy answers with a rate-limit error carrying a retry-after hint. No load reaches the server.
faults.reversal: Instant. Calls resume on the next request; nothing to drain.
faults.limitation: Real providers escalate penalties under sustained abuse; this does not. Treat a pass as a floor, not proof.

faults.name: Server unavailable
faults.simulates: The MCP server process is down or its stdio session dropped.
faults.mechanism: The proxy raises the client's 'not connected' error. The real server keeps running and is not restarted.
faults.reversal: Instant. The server was never actually stopped.
guardrails: High risk: needs approval outside dev
faults.limitation: Does not exercise the real reconnect path; use the Tool servers Reconnect action for that.

faults.name: Malformed output
faults.simulates: A tool that returns something other than its documented result: free text or the wrong structure.
faults.mechanism: The proxy makes the real call, then replaces the result before the agent sees it.
faults.limitation: Only two corruption shapes are generated; subtle wrong-but-valid values are covered by 'Stale data'.

faults.name: Empty result
faults.simulates: A query that silently returns nothing (replication lag, wrong filter, cold cache).
faults.mechanism: The proxy makes the real call and empties every list in the result, keeping its shape valid.
guardrails: Only offered where the response contains collections
faults.limitation: Counts in the payload are not rewritten, which makes the inconsistency easier to spot than in real life.

faults.name: Partial result
faults.simulates: A truncated page or an interrupted query.
faults.mechanism: The proxy makes the real call and keeps only the first share of every list.
faults.limitation: Truncation is uniform; real partial failures are usually skewed to the newest data.

faults.name: Stale data
faults.simulates: A read replica or cache that lags behind the system of record.
faults.mechanism: The proxy makes the real call and drops records newer than the configured age.
guardrails: Only offered where results carry timestamps
faults.limitation: Hides new records rather than serving old versions of the same record.

faults.name: Write timeout · commit uncertain
faults.simulates: A write that commits on the server but whose acknowledgement is lost, so the caller cannot tell.
faults.mechanism: The proxy forwards the call (the write really happens), then reports a timeout to the agent.
faults.reversal: Instant, but the write it let through stays committed. Experiment data is removed in cleanup.
faults.limitation: Only meaningful for tools that write; it proves idempotency rather than durability.

faults.name: Model provider error
faults.simulates: The LLM provider returning an error or a quota refusal.
faults.mechanism: The model gateway raises before the request is sent. No tokens are spent.
guardrails: Only active when a model is configured (not in rule-based mode)
faults.limitation: Does not reproduce partial streaming failures.

faults.name: Model latency
faults.mechanism: The model gateway waits before forwarding each completion request.
guardrails: Delay never exceeds 5 s per completion
faults.limitation: Adds delay per request, not per token.

faults.name: Model degradation
faults.simulates: A model that answers with nothing useful (empty or truncated completion).
faults.mechanism: The model gateway replaces the completion with an empty answer and no tool calls.
guardrails: Only active when a model is configured
faults.limitation: Does not simulate fluent-but-wrong answers; those need evaluation sets, not fault injection.
